answer.text: No circular reports a redshift for GRB 250108A.

The redshift values in the documents (z = 2.197 and z = 0.302) belong to GRB 250108B, which is a different burst, and one circular states that the nearby galaxy at z = 0.302 is unlikely to be physically connected to the GRB.

For GRB 250108A itself, the closest information is that an uncatalogued X-ray source is detected within the estimated 3-sigma SVOM/MXTs error region (98 arcsec) and is above the LSXPS 3-sigma upper limit at this position, and is therefore likely the GRB afterglow.
The X-ray afterglow was later confirmed as the X-ray afterglow of the burst.
